findings.title: Correct the claim that IAM runtimes forward Authorization
findings.body: AgentCore permits Authorization in requestHeaderAllowlist only when a custom JWT authorizer is configured. An A2A or issuer-less runtime using IAM with this unconditional allowlist is rejected during create/update; it does not deploy and forward an unchecked header. This explanation, also added to runtime_stack.py, misrepresents a deployment failure as supported behavior. Document the restriction and the need to condition Authorization forwarding on the JWT authorizer; successful synth does not validate this control-plane constraint.

findings.title: Check verifier execution rather than its presence in source
findings.body: This assertion passes whenever the verifier name appears anywhere, including an unused import or comment. For example, leaving the new import while replacing the identity assignment with user_id = context.identity.sub passes this test and the placeholder test, despite restoring unverified identity access. The new security regression guard therefore does not enforce the behavior its name and failure message promise.

other_major.title: Catch failures when the MCP client actually starts
other_major.body: The try block only constructs an MCPClient; its transport factory, including _fetch_gateway_token(), runs later when Strands starts the client and discovers tools. Agent construction is outside the try block, and invocation is also unguarded, so an unreachable gateway or failed token request fails the research request instead of continuing without tools. Initialize and discover gateway tools within the guarded lifecycle, preserving the client context during successful invocations, and fall back to a tool-free agent on setup failure. Add a test where transport startup or token retrieval raises rather than only mocking create_gateway_mcp_client() to raise.

hits.title: Simulate an actual allowed model rather than a fabricated ARN
hits.body: When agents.allowed_models is configured, the runtime role permits only the specified model and inference-profile ARNs. The fabricated foundation-model/anthropic.claude ARN will not match those permissions, so the guarded simulation returns implicitDeny even when enforcement and real invocations work correctly. Consequently, deploy.sh verify fails when these two security controls are enabled together and incorrectly reports that every agent is broken. Resolve the effective model configuration and simulate the exact model/profile resources the agent invokes.

other_major.title: Validate guardrail compatibility after resolving configuration overrides
other_major.body: The compatibility validator checks only the platform.yaml values, but app.py subsequently resolves agent_pattern and require_guardrails independently from environment variables and CDK context. For example, AGENT_PATTERN=claude-sdk-agent with the security-focused preset passes YAML validation and deploys a Claude SDK runtime with the inference deny but no guardrail attachment. Every inference then fails. This also affects documented environment-variable deployments, not just raw CDK context users. Reject the incompatible combination using the resolved values before constructing the runtime, and cover override combinations in tests.

findings.title: Only check runtime guardrails when the footprint contains a runtime
findings.body: A federated platform account intentionally has no runtime stacks, even when require_guardrails is enabled for the deployment. This unconditional flag check still launches check_guardrail_enforcement.py, which looks up the orchestrator runtime role and fails because that role correctly does not exist in the platform account. Gate this check on the runtime footprint, as the invoke checks already do.

hits.title: Environment export cannot preserve valid values containing commas
hits.body: MigrationSource.env accepts arbitrary string values, but MIGRATION_ENV uses commas both as data and as pair separators without escaping. For example, {'OPTIONS': 'a,b', 'LOG_LEVEL': 'info'} exports as OPTIONS=a,b,LOG_LEVEL=info, which cannot be unambiguously decoded. This makes the new exported contract lossy for ordinary configuration such as lists of endpoints or options.

hits.title: Secret checks report authorization and service failures as missing secrets
hits.body: Every unsuccessful describe-secret call is reported as a missing secret, with stderr discarded and a create-secret command recommended. Valid STS credentials do not imply permission to describe secrets, so AccessDenied, expired credentials, or connectivity failures produce a successful plan with incorrect prerequisite information. Only ResourceNotFoundException should be classified as missing; other failures should be surfaced as failed or inconclusive checks.

other_major.title: Plan claims migration source selects an image before runtime support exists
other_major.body: The plan says agents.pattern is ignored and the runtime image comes from migration.source, but this PR leaves app.py and the runtime stacks unchanged. Deploying the modified migration preset therefore still deploys the selected framework image, not the declared source container; selecting target.runtime: ec2 likewise does not change compute. The operator-facing plan gives a false account of what the current deployment will do.

hits.title: The adapter permanently elevates the customer service to root
hits.body: The Dockerfile switches to root for installation and never switches back, so both the adapter and the original customer command execute as root—even when the source image deliberately uses a non-root user. This violates the platform's non-root container constraint and removes an existing security boundary from migrated services. Capture the source image's configured user during inspection and restore an appropriate non-root runtime user after installation, with a writable HOME.

other_major.title: Unquoted parentheses break the source-build branch
other_major.body: CodeBuild executes this command through a shell, where the unquoted parentheses in `echo Building customer image from source (linux/arm64)...` are syntax rather than ordinary argument text. The build-from-source migration path therefore fails before running the customer image build. Quote the entire echo message.

other_major.title: Forwarding can block indefinitely on a live but stalled child
other_major.body: `urlopen` is called without a timeout, and subsequent response reads use that same unbounded socket. A customer process that accepts a connection but stops responding can therefore hold an invocation indefinitely. The supervisor only detects process exit, so it cannot recover from this state; even if the external caller times out, the adapter's outstanding request remains blocked. Configure bounded connect/read inactivity timeouts suitable for agent execution and streaming, map timeouts to a structured error, and close the response on failures.

hits.title: Successful handoff aborts when the export has no remaining importers
hits.body: When Observability is the export's only consumer, removing its import makes CloudFormation list-imports fail with ValidationError stating that the export is not imported by any stack; it does not return an empty list or 'None'. This verification therefore exits after a successful handoff, before replacing the Runtime. The same problem affects discovery on a retry at line 1363. The regression mock returns 'None' and consequently misses the real AWS behavior.

other_major.title: Targeted retries cannot recover a pending Observability rebind
other_major.body: The rebind depends exclusively on an in-process marker initialized to zero. If a targeted Runtime deployment replaces the Runtime but the subsequent Observability deployment fails or the process terminates, the instructed retry reads the already-updated generation and returns from preparation at line 1333 without setting the marker. Rebinding is then skipped, leaving Observability pinned to the old, deleted Runtime ARN even though the retry reports success. Recovery needs to detect or persist a pending rebind across processes, rather than relying only on this marker.

other_major.title: Lower generations are accepted instead of rejected
other_major.body: This condition returns successfully for both an unchanged generation and a lower requested generation, allowing the subsequent CDK deployment to replace the Runtime with an older generation. Requesting generation 1 bypasses discovery altogether at line 1307. This contradicts the documented prohibition on removing or decrementing generations and the promised fail-before-mutation behavior; with an existing Observability import it can also recreate the export-deletion failure this change is intended to prevent. Discover the deployed generation before the generation-1 shortcut, reject lower values explicitly, and treat equality separately.
